name: Failure Condition Formalization
purpose: Formalize known mathematical failure modes as first-class substrate objects rather than defects to hide.

formal_failure_conditions.definition: Loss of stability in recursive aspect binding where transformation history cannot be bounded.
Recursive actualization of divergent continuations beyond local resource limits.
Inability to find an admissible orientation minimization, blocking selection.
Formal case where Im_A contains zero admissible elements.
Failure of MT-001 under specific adversarial or unstable neighborhood conditions.
Loss of relational equivalence during NavT transport.
Invalid operator composition due to domain/codomain mismatch.
δ fails to return an actualization despite non-null mismatch.

mandatory_rules.rule: Failure is structural information and must be preserved in all formal traces.
Counterexample cases must remain traceable to their original source-relation context.
Formal reconciliation of a failure does not constitute its discharge from the substrate.

governance_rules.rule: Any claim that hides failure modes triggers immediate block of theorem readiness.

forbidden_claims: Failure conditions prove physical entropy laws.
Mathematical divergence justifies the rejection of the framework core.
Reconciliation allows for the assumption of perfect formal closure.
